## 5. WATCH BUT DON'T TRADE

- **AAPL**: Low HV rank (38) with compressed 20.6% IV produces thin premium; 48 DTE to earnings creates awkward timing for 7-14 DTE trades.
- **AMZN**: HV rank 17 with 25.7% IV too low for attractive premium; below 50d MA signals technical weakness.
- **MSFT**: HV rank 20 with only 23.3% IV offers minimal edge; 47 DTE to earnings creates roll complexity.
- **GOOGL**: HV rank 9 (bottom decile) with 18.2% IV produces sub-optimal risk/reward; below both MAs technically concerning.
- **LLY**: Strikes too wide for precision ($5 increments on $1,123 stock); 48 DTE to earnings creates event risk without compensating premium.
- **OKLO**: High-risk flag with 74% IV tempting but extreme volatility (142.9% historical high) creates unpredictable swings; pass for portfolio stability.
- **TEM**: High-risk flag with 115.8% IV screaming bubble territory; HV rank 93 means you're selling at relative highs but absolute risk unacceptable.
- **SHOP**: Elevated IV (51.3%) attractive but below both MAs with 53 DTE to earnings creates technical + event risk combination.
- **GILD**: Inconsistent IV skew across strikes signals pricing inefficiency; 48 DTE to earnings without clear directional bias.

## 7. KEY RISKS / FLAGS

- **Compressed vol regime**: VIX sub-18 with low HV ranks across mega-caps means limited cushion if volatility expands; favor higher-rank names (NVDA 87, HOOD 90) over compressed tickers.
- **Earnings cluster 40-50 DTE**: TSLA (40), AAPL/AMZN/MSFT/LLY (48) create roll/management complexity for Oct expiries; favor 14-21 DTE here to avoid event risk.
- **Technical divergence**: Multiple names (GOOGL, SHOP, AVGO, AMZN) below key MAs signal sector rotation underway; our picks emphasize names above both 50d/200d MAs (TSLA, NVDA, AMD, HOOD, PLTR) or finding support with fat premium (AVGO).
